stem: The fi rst cereal used by man was :
expl: There are mainly eight types of food grains consumed by modern human society, namely barley, wheat, maize, millet, sorghum, mustard, oat and rice. These plants were present in the form of weeds in diff erent areas, which were later grown as seeds by human beings at diff erent places, in diff erent times. Although, barley was the fi rst grain to be cultivated by human beings during 8000 B.C. in western Asian countries located between the northeast Mediterranean Sea and Iran. Later, in the same area, wheat was also cultivated around 8000 B.C.

stem: The earliest evidence of agriculture in Indian subcontinent comes from –
exam: U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004 | U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2008
expl: According to the latest research, the earliest evidence of agriculture in Indian sub-continent has been reported from the Lahuradeva site in Sant Kabir Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh. The evidence of human activity and beginning of rice cultivation at this site dates back to around 8000- 7000 B.C. Signifi cantly before this research, the earlier evidence of wheat was found at Mehrgarh (located in Balochistan, Pakistan) belonging to around 7000 B.C. and the earliest evidence of rice is known to be near the bank of the river Belan, district Prayagraj, from where rice bran was found. With above reference, if Lahuradeva is one option, then it will be the correct answer, but if Lahuradeva is not an option, then Mehrgarh would be the right answer.

stem:
With reference to the cultural heritage of Uttar Pradesh, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
(1) The oldest evidence of agriculture in the global context has been obtained from many excavated sites in this region.
(2) The oldest cultivated food grains are barley and paddy.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below –
Code -
expl: Uttar Pradesh has been blessed with a rich cultural heritage since prehistoric times. It is noteworthy that Koldihwa situated in the Belan River valley region of the state, has been considered to be the oldest evidence of paddy cultivation in the world for a long time. Similarly, Lahuradev, which currently presents the oldest evidence of paddy cultivation, is also a part of Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Hence statement (1) is correct. Evidence of the oldest agricultural grains barley and paddy has been found from many excavated sites of Uttar Pradesh, evidence of barley and paddy has been found from Mahagada and evidence of paddy has been found from Koldihwa.

stem: Ahar or Banas culture was a contemporary of which culture?
expl: The Ahar-Banas culture (2100-1500 BC) was contemporary with the Harappan Civilisation. It fl ourished in the present day Mewar region of Rajasthan, particularly along the Banas River and its tributaries. Ahar, Gilund, Balathal are some of the prominent sites of this culture.

stem: Excavation at Navadatoli was conducted by –
expl: Navdatoli has revealed excellent evidence of both round and rectangular residential structures which are located near Khargone (Madhya Pradesh). The former measures about 1–4.5 m in diameter and the latter 5.6 m long. The roofs were probably made of hay, branches and leaves and were supported on massive wooden posts, 22cm in diameter, raised at regular intervals around the huts. The open spaces between the posts were provided with mud-plastered bamboo screens. The house fl oors were made up of silt clay and river gravel, with the surface coated with lime. The huts were provided with one or two-mouthed ‘chulhas’ as well as storage jars and other earthen vessels. This site was excavated by Mr. H.D. Sankalia, Professor of Deccan College, Pune. This site was the most extensive excavated Chalcolithic site of Indian sub-continent, which is determined to be between 1500 B.C. and 1300 B.C.

stem: Megaliths have been identifi ed as-
expl: The megaliths usually refer to the burials made up of large stones in graveyards away from the habitation area. A large fraction of these is assumed to be associated with burial or post-burial rituals including memorials for those whose remains may or may not be available. Few types of these are; Chamber tombs, Dolmens, Stone alignments, Stone circles (cromlech), Pit-circles, etc.

stem: The Ochre-coloured Pottery (O.C.P.) was christened at:
expl: Discovery and Naming (Christen) of OCP was done by B.B. Lal in 1950-52 at Hastinapur. Ochre-Coloured Pottery (known to archaeologists as OCP) as the name implies, its main distinguishing feature was when rubbed it left on ochre-colour on fi ngers which gives it a fi rst appearance of being badly fi red. Other characteristics are its porous character and the fact that it is invariably worn out at the edges.

stem: In the Chalcolithic period people of Maharashtra buried their dead under the fl oor of their houses in the following orientation:
expl: The people of Jorwe culture lived in large rectangular houses with wattle and daub walls and thatched roofs. They believed in life after death and therefore buried the dead inside the houses under the fl oor. Children were buried in two urns that were joined mouth-to-mouth and set horizontally in the pit, while adults were placed in a supine position with their head towards the north (north to south). These sites were found in Daimabad, Inamgaon, Chandoli, Nevasa etc.

stem: Which of the following sites has yielded skeleton of the dog along with human skeleton in burial ?
expl: The Burzahom site is a prehistoric settlement in the village of the same name in Kashmir Valley. Both human and animal skeletons were found here with trepanning (bored hole) marks. In many pits, bones of dogs and antlered deer were found along with human skeletons. The skeletons of humans were found in the burial pits in a sitting position along with the bones of animals. The fi rst excavation at the Burzahom site was carried out by Helmut de Terra and Dr. Thomas Paterson in 1935 AD.

stem:
Consider the following pairs : (Historical place) (Well-known for)
1. Burzahom Rock-cut shrines
2. Chandra-ketugarh Terracotta art
3. Ganeshwar Copper artefacts
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
expl: Burzahom is a Neolithic site in Kashmir valley. The site is famous for pit dwelling and Neolithic tool industry and not for rock-cut shrines. Hence pair 1 is not correctly matched. Chandraketugarh is located in the West Bengal. In early historic times, Chandraketugarh was connected to the Ganga by the Vidyadhari river and must have been an important centre of trade and possibly also a political centre. Chandraketugarh was a major centre of terracotta craft. Various kinds of artefacts have been found at the site over the years, including coins, pottery, seals and sealings and fi gurines made of ivory, wood and bronze. Hence pair 2 is correctly matched. The Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture was located in Rajasthan. Hundreds of copper objects have been found at this site. Hence pair 3 is correctly matched. Archaeological State Description Site 1. Chandraketugarh Odisha Trading Port town 2. Inamgaon Maharashtra Chalcolithic site 3. Mangadu Kerala Megalithic site 4. Salihundam Andhra Rock-cut Pradesh cave shrines

stem: Consider the following information: In which of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
expl: Chandraketugarh is an archaeological site in the North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal (not in Odisha). The archaeological studies suggest that once the destination was an important trading port city with huge walls. Hence, information given in row 1 is not correctly matched. Inamgaon is a post-Harappan agrarian village and archaeological site located in Pune district of Maharashtra. Inamgaon is one of the most intensively and extensively excavated and well reconstructed Chalcolithic sites of the Deccan plateau. Hence, information given in row 2 is correctly matched. Mangadu is one of the important excavated Megalithic sites in the Kollam district of Kerala. The Megalithic monuments at Mangadu consisted of 28 hard, compact and uneven laterite blocks. The urn-burials at Mangadu reveal the evidence of post-cremation fragmentary burials. Hence, information given in row 3 is correctly matched. Salihundam, is a historically important Buddhist site in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh. There are a number of Buddhist stupas and a huge monastic complex on a hillock amidst scenic surroundings. During excavations relic caskets, four stupas, a Chaityagriha, structural temples and a number of sculptures reflecting the three phases of Buddhism-Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana were found here. However, there is no rock-cut cave shrines found here. Hence, information given in row 4 is not correctly matched. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

stem: Which of these departments/ministries deals with Archaeological Survey of India as an accessory offi ce ?
expl: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), under the Ministry of Culture, is a premier organization for the archaeological research and protection of the cultural heritage of the nation. In 1871, the Archaeological Survey was established as a separate department and Alexander Cunningham was appointed as its fi rst Director-General. In 1901, during the tenure of Lord Curzon, it was centralized and designated as the Archaeological Survey of India. In 1902 John Marshall assumed offi ce of its Director General.
